propositions: A flat per-context character bound (currently 100,000 chars) conflates two independent ceilings: physical model-window capacity and economic per-criterion fan-out cost, causing repeated exhaustion as tickets grow beyond a hand-raised limit.

The bound must be split into two explicit ceilings: a physical ceiling derived from the resolved verifier model's own context window (not escalation max), and an economic ceiling on the product of context_chars × criteria_count.

The current ticket c9f7 (121,147 chars × 22 criteria = 2.67M product) is under the ratified worst-case budget (32 × 100k = 3.2M) yet refused at preflight because the per-axis split is arbitrary, blocking re-certification with no escape except --force-close.

The physical ceiling should be window_tokens × 2 chars/token (conservative estimate leaving headroom for system prompt, criteria, tool traffic, output); for the default claude-sonnet-4-6 model (1M token window) this yields 2M chars, admitting c9f7 with 16.5x safety margin.

The economic ceiling should be _MAX_RECOVERY_INPUT_CHARS = 3_200_000 (byte-identical to the previous worst case, now allocated where real tickets need it) and refuse only when len(context) × len(criteria) exceeds it.

The physical and economic ceilings must be expressed directly in _validate_recovery_inputs with derivations from the resolved model window and the criteria product, replacing the static _MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS constant, while preserving d59e's invariants (no elision, full byte-identical context to model, zero billable calls on refusal).
